adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72-77, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 (also 164,192,237), packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 (also 509) — Office365/Lark/CalDav createEvent (and update/delete) ignore the credentialId param entirely and always destructure destinationCalendar[0], so a collective event with 2+ hosts on the same non-Google provider silently writes every host's event using host-0's calendar externalId while authenticating with each host's own credential, defeating the multi-host feature for 3 of 4 providers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array and updates GoogleCalendarService to select the calendar by matching `credentialId`. However, Office365 and Lark services now destructure only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and use its `externalId` for create/update/delete (Lark: createEvent/createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent; Office365: createEvent). In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the code loops over each destination calendar and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` but passes the same `event` object (with the full destinationCalendar array) to each credential-specific creation. As a result, for non-Google providers, every host’s event creation will use `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` regardless of which host/credential is being used, which can write to the wrong calendar or fail when the authenticated credential doesn’t own that calendar. The finding’s mention of a CalDav file isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the core issue is clearly present for Office365 and Lark in the shown changes.
